question.text: What is 'option premium erosion' (time decay) behavior for ITM vs OTM options?

answer.text: OTM options lose their entire value to time decay if they remain OTM at expiry, since they have no intrinsic value. ITM options lose only their time value component — the intrinsic value portion is preserved
ITM options have the fastest time decay because they are the most expensive
OTM options have no time decay because they have no value to lose
All options decay at the same rate regardless of moneyness

explanation.text: The Logic: Premium equals intrinsic value plus time value. ATM and OTM options have only time value, and time value falls to zero by expiry. So an OTM option, all else equal, loses its entire premium if it is still OTM at expiry. An ITM option keeps its intrinsic value at expiry; only the time-value component decays. The Trap: OTM options do have time value (their entire premium is time value). ITM options are more expensive but a larger share of their premium is intrinsic, not time value. Note: OTM loss to time decay is conditional on the option still being OTM at expiry.
